# Design System: Clean Shopper

**Version:** 1.0  
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-12  
**Source:** Generated by design-system-generator skill from brand interview

---

## How to Use This Document

This file is referenced by CLAUDE.md and read by Claude Code at the start of every session. Apply these tokens for all UI work. Do not hardcode hex values, pixel sizes, or spacing values in components. Reference token names from tailwind.config.js instead.

---

## Brand Direction

Clean Shopper embodies **trustworthy clarity, organic authenticity, informed boldness, and expressive energy**. Like a knowledgeable friend at a farmer's market who speaks with conviction, the app feels approachable, transparent, genuinely helpful, and unapologetically confident. Inspired by holistic organic food brands—transparent, community-driven, and rooted in wellness—the visual language is warm and natural, never clinical or timid. Bold typography and strong color choices convey expertise and decisiveness. Expressive design moments celebrate informed choices and create excitement around discovering clean products. This creates confidence that users are making the right choices for their families.

## Color System

### Primary Colors

| Token Name | Hex Value | Usage Rule |
|---|---|---|
| primary | #2D6A4F | Primary buttons, active navigation states, brand moments. The single most important interactive element per view. Conveys trust, growth, and natural wellness. Never use for decoration or background fills. |
| primary-light | #40916C | Hover states on primary elements, secondary fills, reinforcement moments. Use when primary needs visual feedback without replacing it. |
| primary-dark | #1B4332 | Pressed states, active focus indicators, strong emphasis. Use sparingly for interaction feedback only. |

### Secondary Colors

| Token Name | Hex Value | Usage Rule |
|---|---|---|
| secondary | #F5F1E8 | Secondary background fills, card backgrounds, creates organic warmth. Pair with primary text for readable secondary content areas. |
| secondary-light | #FAF8F3 | Subtle background tints, minimal contrast moments. |

### Accent Colors

| Token Name | Hex Value | Usage Rule |
|---|---|---|
| accent | #D97706 | **Bold highlights**, badges, call-to-action accents, secondary interactive elements. Strong warmth and informed decision-making. Use boldly for elements that need attention—don't be timid with this color. Accent buttons, important badges, featured products. |
| accent-light | #F59E0B | Hover states for accent elements, secondary highlights, alternative interactive feedback. Creates expressive interaction feedback. |
| accent-bold | #C65D00 | Pressed states, strong emphasis on accent elements, alternative primary CTAs. Maximum boldness for accent moments. |

### Semantic Colors

| Token Name | Hex Value | Usage Rule |
|---|---|---|
| success | #10D981 | Product is clean/safe, positive confirmations, ingredient passes safety checks, verified badges, checkmarks. Carry meaning—never use for decoration. Bold, vibrant green for confident affirmation. |
| warning | #FBBF24 | Ingredient requires attention, unverified claims, "review this" moments, caution states. Signals need for user review, not danger. Bold, vibrant amber for clear visibility. |
| error | #F97316 | Harmful ingredient detected, safety concern, ingredient to avoid, destructive actions. Reserved for genuine safety issues, not minor warnings. Bold, vibrant orange-red for immediate attention. |

### Neutral Colors

| Token Name | Hex Value | Usage Rule |
|---|---|---|
| neutral-50 | #FEFDFB | Page background, creates calm, organic foundation throughout the app. |
| neutral-100 | #F9FAFB | Card backgrounds, surface fills, subtle contrast from page background. |
| neutral-200 | #E5E7EB | Borders, dividers, visual separation between elements. Barely visible—restraint is key. |
| neutral-400 | #9CA3AF | Placeholder text, disabled states, de-emphasized content. |
| neutral-600 | #6B7280 | Secondary text, supporting copy, metadata, less critical information. |
| neutral-900 | #1F2937 | Primary text, headings, strongest contrast. Never use pure black (#000000). |

## Typography

**Font Family:** Inter (Google Fonts) — Clean, modern, accessible sans-serif. Balances warmth with clarity. Chosen for legibility and contemporary feel that signals a trustworthy, informed tool.

**Source:** Google Fonts (loaded via link tag)

### Type Scale

| Token Name | Size | Weight | Line Height | Usage Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| display | 56px | 800 | 1.1 | Hero headlines, marketing moments, page entry points. Use sparingly—only the most important moment per view. Extra bold for maximum impact. |
| display-sm | 48px | 700 | 1.2 | Large section headers, campaign moments. Bold and expressive without being overwhelming. |
| h1 | 42px | 700 | 1.2 | Main page titles, primary headlines. Sets the context with authority. Bold conveys confidence. |
| h2 | 32px | 700 | 1.3 | Section headers, major content divisions, search results titles. Visual hierarchy checkpoint with strong presence. |
| h3 | 24px | 600 | 1.4 | Card titles, subsection headers, product names. Readable at smaller scale while maintaining boldness. |
| h4 | 18px | 600 | 1.5 | Labels, button text, small headers, form field labels. Direct, confident instruction. |
| body | 16px | 400 | 1.6 | Body copy, descriptions, product details, explanatory text. Default for readable content. Generous line height for scannability. |
| body-bold | 16px | 600 | 1.6 | Emphasized body copy, important callouts, key information. Bold for distinction without changing size. |
| small | 14px | 400 | 1.5 | Supporting text, metadata, tags, timestamps, ingredient lists. Secondary information that complements body. |
| micro | 12px | 400 | 1.4 | Legal text, timestamps, footer content, minimal UI. Smallest readable size; use only for non-critical information. |

## Spacing Scale

Base unit: 8px

| Token Name | Value | Usage Rule |
|---|---|---|
| space-xs | 8px | Icon padding, tight internal spacing within components. Minimal breathing room. |
| space-sm | 16px | Compact padding within buttons and small components. Input field padding. |
| space-md | 24px | Standard internal component padding. Gap between form fields. Default spacing choice. |
| space-lg | 32px | Card padding, section internal spacing. Comfortable padding for read-heavy areas. |
| space-xl | 48px | Gap between components on a page, section margins. Breathing room between distinct content blocks. |
| space-2xl | 64px | Gap between major sections, page section breaks. Visually separates conceptually different areas. |
| space-3xl | 96px | Page-level margins, large section gaps, hero section spacing. Top-level breathing room. |
| space-4xl | 128px | Full-bleed spacing, hero sections, maximum page margins. Reserve for the largest content divisions. |

| Token Name | Value | Usage Rule |

| shadow-sm | 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) | Subtle card lift, resting state, minimal elevation. Restraint for calm moments. |
| shadow-md | 0 4px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) | Hover states, dropdown menus, moderate elevation. Active interaction feedback. |

## Usage Rules Summary

These rules apply to every component built for Clean Shopper:

1. **Never hardcode a hex value.** Use the token name from tailwind.config.js. This keeps the system consistent and maintainable.

2. **Never hardcode a pixel font size.** Use the type scale token classes (display, h1, h2, body, small, micro). The scale maintains hierarchy and readability. Headlines should feel bold and confident.

3. **Never hardcode spacing.** Use the spacing scale token classes (space-xs through space-4xl). Consistency in spacing reinforces calm and intention.

4. **Primary color is for the single most important interactive element per view.** Every screen should have one clear primary action. Be bold about making it prominent. Secondary and accent colors handle everything else.

5. **Use accent color boldly.** Don't be timid with #D97706. Featured products, important badges, secondary CTAs, and expressive moments should use accent color prominently. Accent boldness conveys expertise and confidence.

6. **Neutral-900 for primary text. Neutral-600 for secondary text.** Never use pure black (#000000) or pure white. These create harsh contrast that feels clinical and aggressive—contrary to Clean Shopper's warm, organic feeling.

7. **Semantic colors carry meaning. Do not use success green for anything other than positive/safe states.** Warning amber only for caution moments. Error red only for genuine harm or destructive actions. Misuse confuses users about product safety.

8. **Typography should feel bold and expressive.** Use weight-700 for headers (display, h1, h2) to create strong visual hierarchy. Weight-600 for subheaders (h3, h4). Use body-bold for emphasized information. Never set body copy smaller than 16px. Use adequate line height (1.6 for body, 1.5 for supporting text).

9. **Shadows add dimension and expressiveness.** Default to shadow-md for interactive elements (buttons, cards). Use shadow-lg for hover states. Use shadow-xl for expressive moments and featured content. Avoid shadow-sm for primary interactive elements—they need more presence.

10. **Spacing reflects calm and intention.** Use generous whitespace to create breathing room. Information density should feel manageable. Don't crowd expressive moments—give them space to breathe.

11. **The secondary color (#F5F1E8) is intentional.** This warm cream background reinforces the "organic" brand direction. Use it for cards and secondary content areas to create warmth without using primary color too broadly.

12. **Be bold and expressive.** This is not a timid app. Confident typography, strong colors, and purposeful spacing convey expertise. Celebrate informed choices with visual delight.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

### WCAG AA Compliance (Required)

**Text Color Contrast Ratios** (4.5:1 minimum for body text, 3:1 for large text)

| Text Color | Background | Ratio | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| neutral-900 (#1F2937) | neutral-50 (#FEFDFB) | 15.8:1 | ✅ Pass |
| neutral-900 (#1F2937) | secondary (#F5F1E8) | 14.2:1 | ✅ Pass |
| neutral-600 (#6B7280) | neutral-50 (#FEFDFB) | 8.1:1 | ✅ Pass |
| success (#10D981) | white (#FFFFFF) | 3.8:1 | ⚠️ Large text only |
| warning (#FBBF24) | white (#FFFFFF) | 2.1:1 | ❌ Fails - Use with dark text or background |
| error (#F97316) | white (#FFFFFF) | 6.2:1 | ✅ Pass |
| primary (#2D6A4F) | white (#FFFFFF) | 5.1:1 | ✅ Pass |
| accent (#D97706) | white (#FFFFFF) | 4.1:1 | ✅ Pass |

**Note on Warning Color:** The warning color (#FBBF24) requires darker text or a background tint to meet WCAG AA. Use:
- Dark text on warning background (neutral-900 text on #FBBF24 bg)
- OR add a background tint: #FEF3C7 (light yellow) with neutral-900 text

### Accessibility Standards

- ✅ All text/background combinations must meet WCAG AA contrast ratios (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text)
- ✅ Color must never be the only indicator of state. Use text labels, icons, or patterns in addition to color
- ✅ Interactive elements must be at least 44px × 44px for touch targets (or 24px if nested)
- ✅ Use semantic HTML heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3, never skip levels)
- ✅ All interactive elements must be keyboard accessible (Tab, Enter, Space, Arrow keys)
- ✅ Form inputs must have associated labels, not just placeholder text
- ✅ Provide alt text for all images and icons
- ✅ Use ARIA labels for icon-only buttons
- ✅ Ensure focus indicators are visible (minimum 2px, high contrast)
- ✅ Test in both light and dark contexts where applicable
- ✅ Use sufficient line-height (1.5 minimum) for readability
- ✅ Avoid pure black (#000000) and pure white (#FFFFFF) — they create harsh contrast
